minutes.headline: Town Meeting passed TC Passios design money and Brooks House sale; marijuana setback raised to 500 feet.
minutes.summary: Town Meeting handled the Brooks House land and building conveyance articles, design and engineering money for the TC Passios building, and the start of the marijuana bylaw. The discovery that the prohibition questions were not on the May ballot shaped the marijuana debate. A setback amendment passed, and a further amendment to bar marijuana from residential districts was still being debated when the captions end.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting passed article 24, a transfer from free cash for design and engineering of the TC Passios building, on a counted show of cards by simple majority.
Articles 22 and 23, conveying the Brooks House land and the building, each passed by two-thirds after amendments to limit the land, bar demolition and add a time limit failed.
A discovery that the marijuana prohibition questions were not on the May ballot led town counsel to advise that articles 26 to 31 could proceed, with a special election to follow.
An amendment raising the residential setback for marijuana establishments from 375 to 500 feet passed.
A further amendment to bar marijuana from residential districts was still being debated when the captions end, so article 25 was undecided.

why_it_matters: Article 24 draws on free cash, which is town money that could otherwise serve other needs, and the design estimate covered only part of the design fee, so later design costs are still to come.

The Brooks House votes decide whether a parcel near the library, TCP and schools leaves town ownership, and the marijuana setback and ballot error affect where such businesses may locate and which questions voters will face at a special election.
